title: Symmetry cancels returns in networks of loops; a shared ring with more contacts does not
claim: In a network of rule-60 rings joined by contacts with law (12, 12), every ring with at least two contacts and consecutive contacts at least two cells apart: (1) a contact c keeps its two chain-end witnesses at every lag exactly when D_cc = 1, D = (I + K)^-1 for the weighted contact graph (corner weights z a^l, a = z/(1+z)), i.e. when its returns cancel, and then binds both rings at every lag; (2) the positions embed the ring graph in an oriented surface whose rings and faces are the contact graph's closed routes, and in a uniform network (equally spaced, or on the sphere with every ring and face of one density) D_cc = 1 iff every count of returns to c is even; (3) an automorphism fixing c and exchanging its out-arcs cancels its returns, so every orientably regular map built as a uniform network (loops, two rings sharing m contacts, the Platonic networks, square, triangular and honeycomb lattices of rings on a torus) keeps every contact persistent at every lag at every size; (4) a contact joining a ring of two contacts to a ring of three or more, with no two-contact face, has exactly one return of length 2, so in a uniform network its witnesses lapse, first at lag 2(density) + 1; figure-eights and chords across loops have such contacts.
failure_conditions: A network and contact with D_cc = 1 whose chain-end witness has coefficient 0 at some lag, or D_cc != 1 with no lapse at val(D_cc - 1) + 1.
A regular uniform network with a contact whose return counts are not all even or that misses a ring at some lag.
A contact meeting Theorem 4's hypothesis with N_2 != 1.
foundation_claim_scope: Linear networks of rule-60 rings with law (12, 12) contacts; two-time knots only (A30); no distance.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's standing request on 2026-11-08.
validation.status: proof by hand; finite claims checked by check.py
validation.novelty: known-with-delta: persistence across time is the cancellation of returns in the directed medial graph of the embedding the positions define; edge-reversing map symmetries cancel them, and a ring of two contacts meeting a larger ring leaves one return of length 2 unpaired
